docs.title: NewUU Documentation Template
docs.text:
The documentation template of the School of Engineering, New Uzbekistan University. Clone it, replace the content, and the design is already done — colours, typography, components and accessibility are decided and written down.

Start here See every component

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A decided visual system

    NewUU navy and green, a navy-tinted neutral ramp, and a light and a dark scheme that were designed separately rather than one being a filter of the other. Every choice is recorded in DESIGN-DECISIONS.md.

  • A component vocabulary

    Tables, a three-step admonition ladder, keyboard keys, step sequences, card grids, tabs, code blocks and status pills — each with copy-paste source on the Components page.

  • Three languages

    English, Russian and Uzbek through mkdocs-static-i18n, with fallback to English for pages that are not translated yet.

  • Accessible by construction

    Every colour that carries text meets WCAG AA against its own background, and severity is never signalled by colour alone.

docs.title: Start a new documentation repository
docs.text:
1. Use this repository as a template. On GitHub, press Use this template → Create a new repository, inside the NewUU-engineering organisation.

  2. Change the five values under CHANGE THESE at the top of mkdocs.yml: site_name, site_description, site_url, repo_url, repo_name.

  3. Replace the content. Delete docs/guide/ and docs/example/, write your own pages, and rewrite nav.

  4. Push to main. The Deploy docs workflow publishes to GitHub Pages by itself. Enable Pages once, from the gh-pages branch.

The template keeps the design decisions, not your content

docs/guide/ and docs/example/ exist to show what is available. Once your own documentation is written, delete them — the theme does not depend on them.

docs.title: Example section
docs.text:
Two pages showing the components doing real work rather than being demonstrated. Delete this section when you write your own.

  • Example procedure

    A safety-and-operation page: danger callout, decision table with a marked emergency row, step sequence, tabbed code.

  • Example reference

    A specification page: dense tables, definition lists, footnotes, abbreviations.

This page is a section index

navigation.indexes lets a section have its own landing page. The file is example/index.md and it appears in nav as the first entry of the section.

docs.title: Example procedure
docs.text:
Stable

Run through this page before every session.

Before every session

Confirm the emergency stop combination with every person present, and keep 2 m of clear floor around the equipment at all times.

docs.title: How to stop the unit
docs.text:
There is no physical emergency stop on this configuration. Stopping is a remote action, and the correct action depends on the situation.

Situation Action Result Moving somewhere unintended, situation under control 1× START Returns to standing and holds A sequence is running and must be cut short 2× START The running sequence is interrupted Emergency: unpredictable behaviour, risk to people L2+B Damping mode — the unit slowly sinks to the ground Controller dead or unresponsive Battery button Only after the unit is suspended, feet clear of the ground, 2 m of clear space

A double press is not an emergency stop

Double-press interrupts whatever is currently running. If nothing is running, the unit steps in place — and the operator believes they pressed stop.

Fall protection is not a stop

Fall protection switches the motors to braking. It reduces damage; it does not replace correct stopping procedure.

docs.title: Pre-session procedure
docs.text:
1. Clear the workspace. At least 2 m of clear floor around the unit. Dry, hard, level surface only.

  2. Confirm the stop combination with every participant. Each person present says the combination aloud: L2+B

  3. Check the battery. Below 20 % the unit may sit down without warning.

    Do not begin a session below 20 %

    Charge first. A shutdown mid-session drops the unit from standing height.

  4. Record the session. Date, operator, unit serial number.

docs.title: Confirming state from the SDK
Session checklist
docs.text:
• Workspace cleared to 2 m
  • Stop combination confirmed aloud by every participant
  • Battery above 20 %
  • Session recorded in the log

docs.title: Example reference
docs.text:
Draft

A specification page: dense tables, definitions, and notes that belong at the foot rather than in the flow.

docs.title: Operating limits
docs.text: Parameter Value Notes Operating temperature 0 – 40 °C Below 0 °C the battery will not charge Continuous runtime 90 min At 20 °C with a full charge<sup>1</sup> Maximum payload 3 kg Distributed; a point load derates this sharply Minimum clear space 2 m radius Non-negotiable during any session Charge time 2 h 0 → 100 % with the supplied charger Network 1 Gb Ethernet SDK requires a wired link

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Damping mode Motors are energised but compliant. The unit sinks under its own weight rather than falling. This is the safe stop state. Suspended Held on the gantry with the feet clear of the ground. Required before any power cycle. Idle Powered, balanced, holding position, accepting commands.

docs.title: Controller reference
docs.text:
Input Function START Return to idle 2× START Interrupt running sequence L2+B Emergency: damping mode L1+A Cycle operating mode SELECT Toggle fall protection

Keep this table in sync with the controller

If the firmware remaps an input, this table is the page that will be wrong. Reference it from procedures rather than repeating the combinations.

The SDK exposes the same commands over Ethernet.

  1. Measured at 20 °C on a battery under 50 charge cycles. Expect roughly 15 % less in the first session after storage. ↩

docs.title: Using this template
docs.text:
This section is the reference for the template itself. Delete it once your own documentation is written — the theme does not depend on it.

  • Components

    Every element the theme styles, rendered, with copy-paste source.

  • Writing style

    How to write procedures that hold up when somebody is reading them mid-task.

  • Translations

    How the English, Russian and Uzbek versions of a page fit together.

docs.title: Running the site locally
docs.text:
1. Create a virtual environment and install the dependencies.

    python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

  2. Serve with live reload.

    mkdocs serve

    The site is then at http://127.0.0.1:8000. Saved edits reload the page.

  3. Check the build is clean before pushing.

    mkdocs build --strict

    --strict turns broken links and missing files into errors. CI runs it, so a clean local build means a green pipeline.

Docker, if you prefer

docker run --rm -it -p 8000:8000 -v ${PWD}:/docs squidfunk/mkdocs-material

Note that the i18n plugin is not in that image — install it in the container or use the virtual environment for translated sites.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md              landing page
│   ├── assets/               logos, favicon, images
│   ├── stylesheets/
│   │   └── newuu.css         the theme — do not edit casually
│   ├── includes/             shared snippets pulled in with --8<--
│   ├── guide/                this section — delete it
│   └── example/              example pages — delete them
├── .github/

docs.title: Changing the theme
docs.text:
Don't, casually. The value of a template is that the same decisions are not remade in every repository — and newuu.css encodes decisions that were made against measured contrast ratios, not taste.

If a genuine gap appears, open an issue against the template repository so that the fix reaches every site, rather than patching one repository's stylesheet.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Every element the theme styles, rendered, with the source underneath. Copy from here rather than inventing — that is the whole point of the template.

Toggle the theme with the icon in the header: every component below is designed in both schemes, not filtered.

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text:
Three severities, and each carries a distinct shape as well as a colour, so the ladder survives greyscale and every form of colour blindness.

Emergency stop

The one component that must be impossible to skim past. Filled title bar, 4px edge, circle-and-bang icon.

The emergency combination is L2+B — and it belongs in the body, not the title. See the note below.

Use danger only where ignoring it can injure somebody or destroy equipment. If everything is a danger, nothing is.

This is a warning

For things that will cost time, money or data — but not safety. Triangle icon, amber, no filled bar.

This is a note

Context, background, a useful aside. Plain green rule, no ground. note is the only content component allowed to use the brand green.

Collapsed danger — click to open

Admonitions collapse with ??? instead of !!!. Add a trailing + — ???+ — to render it open but collapsible.

Tables and code blocks nest inside without breaking the frame.

Source
!!! danger "Emergency stop"

    Indent the body by four spaces.

!!! warning "This is a warning"

    Body text.

!!! note "This is a note"

    Body text.

??? danger "Collapsed danger — click to open"

    `???` collapses, `???+` renders open but collapsible.

Keyboard keys do not work in an admonition title

A title is taken as plain text, so ++l2+b++ written there is published literally as ++l2+b++ — which on a safety callout is exactly the wrong place to be wrong.

Put the combination in the body of the callout. The same applies to summary on a collapsed block.

Do not add admonition types

The theme sanctions exactly three: danger, warning, note. Material ships twelve, and the other nine are deliberately unstyled. A ladder with three rungs is one people can actually read.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
The component that carries these sites. Ruled rather than zebra-striped: at 50+ rows of prose, alternating fills add noise without adding structure.

Situation Action Result Routine stop, situation under control 1× Enter The unit returns to idle A running sequence must be cut short 2× Enter The sequence is interrupted Emergency: risk to people L2+B Damping mode — the unit sinks to the ground Controller unresponsive Battery button Only after the unit is suspended with 2 m of clear space Source
| Situation | Action | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routine stop, situation under control | 1× ++enter++ | The unit returns to idle |
| **Emergency: risk to people** {: .row-danger } | ++l2+b++{: .kbd-danger } | Damping mode |

Why the class goes on the first cell

python-markdown's attr_list does not support attributes on a table row — {: .row-danger } written after a row is emitted as a literal extra cell. It does work on a cell, so the class goes on the row's first cell and CSS lifts it to the whole row with :has().

On mobile the table scrolls horizontally with the first column pinned. Narrow this window below 768px to see it. Collapsing rows into cards was considered and rejected — a 50-row table becomes unnavigable as 50 stacked blocks.

docs.title: Keyboard keys
docs.text:
Controller and keyboard input renders as real keys, not as inline code, so it reads as a button rather than as a filename.

Press Ctrl+Alt+Del to interrupt. A single Enter returns to idle. The emergency combination is L2+B.

Source
Press ++ctrl+alt+del++ to interrupt. A single ++enter++ returns to idle.
The emergency combination is ++l2+b++{: .kbd-danger }.

.kbd-danger inherits the danger colours — use it only for the emergency combination, so that the combination looks the same everywhere it appears.

docs.title: Step sequences
docs.text:
For procedures. Numbered markers, a connecting rule, and room for a warning or a key combination inside any step.

  1. Clear the workspace. At least 2 m of clear floor. Dry, hard, level surface only.

  2. Confirm the stop combination with everyone present. Each person says the combination aloud: L2+B

  3. Check the battery. Below 20 % the unit may shut down without warning.

    Do not start a session below 20 %

    Callouts nest inside a step and keep the connecting rule.

  4. Log the session. Date, operator, and the serial number of the unit.

Source
<div class="steps" markdown>

1.  **Clear the workspace.** At least 2 m of clear floor.

2.  **Confirm the stop combination.** ++l2+b++{: .kbd-danger }

    !!! warning "Callouts nest inside a step"

        Indent by four spaces, as usual.

</div>

The blank line after <div ... markdown> and before </div> is required — without it, md_in_html does not process the contents.

docs.title: Card grids
docs.text:
For landing pages and section indexes. Not for use inside a procedure.

  • A card with an icon

    The --- produces the rule under the title. Icons come from the Material icon set via pymdownx.emoji.

  • A card that links

    Ending a card with a link makes the whole card feel clickable.

    Components reference

Source
<div class="grid cards" markdown>

-   :material-book-open-variant: **A card with an icon**

    ---

    Body text.

-   :material-shield-check: **A card that links**

    ---

    [Components reference](components.md)

</div>

docs.title: Code
Headings
docs.text: h1 opens the page and there is exactly one. h2 takes a rule, h3 and h4 do not. Below h4 the hierarchy has failed — split the page instead.

docs.title: Emphasis, links, quotes
docs.text:
Body text is IBM Plex Sans at weight 500, carried over from the university's own typography. Bold for the operative word in a procedure, italic for quoted source material, and links in blue rather than green.

A blockquote takes the green rule — the same vertical device as the mark. Use it for quoted source material, such as a manufacturer's manual.

  • An outstanding task
Term A definition list. Useful for glossaries and parameter references. Another term With its own definition.

docs.text:

docs.title: Shared snippets
docs.text:
Text repeated across pages should live in docs/includes/ and be pulled in, so that correcting it once corrects it everywhere. The block below is included, not typed:

Before every session

Confirm the emergency stop combination with every person present, and keep 2 m of clear floor around the equipment at all times.

Source
!!! danger "Before every session"

    Confirm the emergency stop combination with every person present, and keep
    2 m of clear floor around the equipment at all times.

Safety warnings duplicated by hand drift apart. This is the fix.

docs.title: What is deliberately absent
docs.text:
Not included Why The other nine admonition types Three rungs is a ladder people can read Zebra-striped tables Noise at 50+ rows of prose Gradients in content Reserved for the landing hero Green as a meaning-carrying colour in content It is what keeps the danger red free Custom fonts beyond the two Every extra weight is a download on a slow connection

  1. Defined anywhere in the file with [^1]: text. ↩

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: The site builds in English, Russian and Uzbek through mkdocs-static-i18n, using the suffix structure.

docs.title: How a page maps to its translations
docs.text:
docs/example/procedure.md        English   (the source of truth)
docs/example/procedure.ru.md     Russian
docs/example/procedure.uz.md     Uzbek

A missing translation falls back to English rather than breaking the build (fallback_to_default: true). That is deliberate: a partial translation should never block publishing.

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
1. English first. Make substantive changes to the English page, then mirror them. A Russian page that has drifted ahead of its English source is a page nobody can review.

  2. Translate the whole page or none of it. A half-translated page is worse than an English one, because the reader cannot tell what they are missing.

  3. Never translate exact input. L2+B is L2+B in every language. Neither are file paths, command names or code.

  4. Keep the file structure identical. Same headings, same order, same tables. Translations are reviewed by comparing them side by side.

Uzbek needs Latin Extended, not plain ASCII

oʻ and gʻ use the modifier letter turned comma (U+02BB), not an apostrophe. IBM Plex Sans covers it; a font without Latin Extended will substitute and the page will look broken.

Why navigation.instant is off

Material's instant loading breaks the language switcher: it sends the reader to the home page of the other language instead of the same page. Do not turn it on. The comment in mkdocs.yml says so too.

docs.title: Marking incomplete coverage
docs.text:
If a language is only partly translated, say so where the reader will see it — at the top of the page, not only in the switcher:

!!! note "Частичный перевод"

    Эта страница ещё не переведена полностью. Разделы без перевода
    отображаются на английском языке.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text: These sites are read by somebody standing next to equipment, looking for one specific step. Write for that reader.

docs.title: Procedures
docs.text:
1. Number every step, and put the action first. "Press Enter to return to idle", not "To return to idle, press Enter". The reader is scanning for the verb.

  2. Be exact about input. L2+B, not "the stop combination". Exact combinations belong in keyboard keys, never in prose.

  3. Say what should happen. A step without an observable result cannot be verified, and the reader cannot tell whether it worked.

  4. One action per step. If a step contains "and", it is usually two steps.

docs.title: Severity
docs.text:
Use When Example danger Ignoring it can injure somebody or destroy equipment Emergency stop combination warning Ignoring it costs time, money or data "Double-press is not an emergency stop" note Context that helps but is not required "Fall protection reduces damage; it does not replace procedure"

Severity inflation is the failure mode

Every callout marked danger makes the next one less visible. On a page with forty callouts, the reader stops seeing all of them.

docs.title: Tone
docs.text:
• Imperative and unambiguous. "Clear 2 m around the unit." Not "the workspace should ideally be clear."
  • No hedging in safety text. "Below 20 % the unit may shut down without warning" is a fact. "It is recommended to check the battery" is not.
  • Numbers with units, always. 2 m, 20 %, 24 V.
  • Name things the way the equipment names them. If the controller says START, write START — not "the start button".

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• One h1, at the top. nav supplies the page title elsewhere.
  • If you reach h5, the page is doing two jobs — split it.
  • Put the safety content before the procedure, not after it.
  • A page that is mostly a table should be a table. Do not narrate a table.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: English is the source of truth. Make substantive changes in English first, then mirror them — see Translations.

docs.title: Part A — Human Motion to Robot
docs.text:
Use UltimateBots Studio to generate a motion for the Unitree G1 robot. You can either upload a short human motion video or describe the motion using a text prompt. Keep the motion under 30 seconds and export it as a LAFAN CSV file.

Then, using the Unitree G1 model from the Unitree RL Gym repository, write a Python script that loads the robot in MuJoCo, plays the generated motion, and renders the result as an MP4 video.

Submit:

  • The rendered robot motion (motion.mp4)
  • The source video or text prompt used
  • The LAFAN motion file (motion.csv)
  • Your Python script and a short README explaining how to reproduce the result

In the README, briefly answer:

  1. How did you determine what the columns in the CSV represent?

docs.title: Part B — Walking Policy
docs.text:
Clone the Unitree RL Gym repository and run the pretrained G1 walking policy using its MuJoCo deployment.

The default policy makes the robot walk forward. Modify the setup so that the robot instead walks in a circle.

Submit:

  • A video of the G1 walking in a circle
  • A short note explaining what you changed and why it produces circular motion

In the note, briefly answer:

  1. What inputs does the policy receive, and where do they come from?
  2. What does the policy output, and how is that converted into joint torques?

docs.title: Links
docs.text:
• UltimateBots Studio: https://studio.ultimatebots.com/home
  • Unitree RL Gym repository: https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_gym

docs.title: Task 2 — Senior Track
docs.text:
Training a locomotion policy in Isaac Lab, then investigating what a change to the task makes.

If you cannot get Isaac Lab running after a reasonable attempt, email us and explain why it didnt work.

docs.title: Part A — Train a walking policy
docs.text:
Install Isaac Lab by following the official installation guide at https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/

Train the Unitree Go2 quadruped on the flat-terrain velocity tracking task that ships with Isaac Lab. Use the default settings. Training runs headless, without a visualizer, and should take a few minutes.

When training finishes, load your trained policy and watch it run in the Newton visualizer. Record the screen.

Submit:

  • A video of your policy running
  • Your trained checkpoint file

docs.title: Part B — Widen the command range and investigate
docs.text:
During training, the policy is given velocity commands sampled from a range. By default the linear velocity range is roughly minus one to plus one metre per second. Find where this range is set in the configuration and widen it to minus two to plus two.

Before you run the training, write down what you expect to happen and why. Put this in your report. If the result contradicts your prediction, say so and explain what you had wrong. A wrong prediction that is honestly analysed scores higher than a correct one with no reasoning behind it.

Retrain with the wider range, then watch the new policy in the visualizer and record it.

Open TensorBoard and compare your two runs. Look at error_vel_xy, success_rate, and the base contact termination rate.

Then retrain the wide-range configuration again, this time with roughly three times as many training iterations, and compare a third time.

Submit:

  • A video and checkpoint for the wide-range policy
  • A video and checkpoint for the wide-range policy trained longer
  • A short report

In the report, answer:

  1. Your prediction, written before you ran the experiment.
  2. What actually happened, with the metrics to support it.
  3. Did more training iterations fix it? If yes, what does that tell you about the cause? If no, what does that rule out?

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Training with the default number of parallel environments takes a few minutes. If you run out of memory, reduce it — but be aware that the number of environments and the number of iterations are coupled, because one iteration collects a batch of data across all environments at once. A run with eight times fewer environments sees eight times less data over the same number of iterations.

docs.title: Пример процедуры
docs.text:
Стабильно

Пройдите эту страницу перед каждым занятием.

Перед каждым занятием

Подтвердите комбинацию аварийной остановки со всеми присутствующими и обеспечьте 2 м свободного пола вокруг оборудования.

docs.title: Как остановить устройство
docs.text:
Физической кнопки аварийной остановки в этой конфигурации нет. Остановка — это действие с пульта, и правильное действие зависит от ситуации.

Ситуация Действие Результат Движется не туда, ситуация под контролем 1× START Возвращается в стойку и удерживает её Выполняется последовательность, нужно прервать 2× START Последовательность прерывается Аварийная ситуация: риск для людей L2+B Режим демпфирования — устройство медленно опускается на пол Пульт не отвечает Кнопка батареи Только после подвешивания, ноги над полом, 2 м свободного пространства

Двойное нажатие — не аварийная остановка

Двойное нажатие прерывает текущее действие. Если ничего не выполняется, устройство шагает на месте — а оператор считает, что нажал стоп.

docs.title: Процедура перед занятием
docs.text:
1. Освободите рабочее место. Не менее 2 м свободного пола вокруг устройства. Только сухая, твёрдая, ровная поверхность.

  2. Подтвердите комбинацию остановки с каждым участником. Каждый присутствующий произносит комбинацию вслух: L2+B

  3. Проверьте батарею. Ниже 20 % устройство может сесть без предупреждения.

  4. Запишите занятие. Дата, оператор, серийный номер устройства.

docs.title: Protsedura namunasi
docs.text:
Barqaror

Har bir mashgʻulotdan oldin ushbu sahifani koʻrib chiqing.

Har bir mashgʻulotdan oldin

Favqulodda toʻxtatish kombinatsiyasini barcha ishtirokchilar bilan tasdiqlang va uskuna atrofida 2 m boʻsh joy taʼminlang.

docs.title: Qurilmani qanday toʻxtatish kerak
docs.text:
Ushbu konfiguratsiyada jismoniy favqulodda toʻxtatish tugmasi yoʻq. Toʻxtatish — bu masofadan boshqarish amali va toʻgʻri amal vaziyatga bogʻliq.

Vaziyat Amal Natija Notoʻgʻri yoʻnalishda harakatlanmoqda, vaziyat nazorat ostida 1× START Turgan holatga qaytadi Ketma-ketlik bajarilmoqda, uzish kerak 2× START Ketma-ketlik uziladi Favqulodda vaziyat: odamlar uchun xavf L2+B Dempferlash rejimi — qurilma sekin yerga tushadi Pult javob bermayapti Batareya tugmasi Faqat qurilma osib qoʻyilgandan soʻng, 2 m boʻsh joy bilan

Ikki marta bosish favqulodda toʻxtatish emas

Ikki marta bosish joriy amalni uzadi. Agar hech narsa bajarilmayotgan boʻlsa, qurilma joyida qadam tashlaydi — operator esa toʻxtatdim deb oʻylaydi.

docs.title: Mashgʻulotdan oldingi protsedura
docs.text:
1. Ish joyini tozalang. Qurilma atrofida kamida 2 m boʻsh pol. Faqat quruq, qattiq, tekis yuza.

  2. Toʻxtatish kombinatsiyasini har bir ishtirokchi bilan tasdiqlang. Har bir ishtirokchi kombinatsiyani ovoz chiqarib aytadi: L2+B

  3. Batareyani tekshiring. 20 % dan past boʻlsa qurilma ogohlantirishsiz oʻtirib qolishi mumkin.

  4. Mashgʻulotni qayd eting. Sana, operator, qurilma seriya raqami.
